title: HyperET: Efficient Training in Hyperbolic Space for Multi-modal Large Langu

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The appendix restates Theorem 1 but inserts the claim 'However, this relation does not strictly hold due to nonlinearities in Möbius multiplication, meaning precise control over radius via scalar multiplication is not guaranteed,' directly contradicting the main-text Theorem 1's claim that 's · Rad_X = Rad_{s⊗_c X}' holds exactly. The very proof given immediately after in the appendix (Eq. 19) derives the equality exactly and without approximation, confirming the main-text theorem is correct and the inserted 'flawed' claim is false and self-contradictory within the same section.

Eq. (11) asserts exp_0^{D,c}(Y_0) = exp_0^{D,c}(W_0 X) = W_0^{D} X^{D} = exp_0^{D,c}(W_0)·exp_0^{D,c}(X), i.e., that the exponential map distributes over matrix multiplication. But per the definition in Eq. (16)/Appendix A, the exponential map is a nonlinear function of the full vector norm (via tanh), so exp_0(W_0 X) cannot generally be factored as exp_0(W_0) times exp_0(X); this step is unjustified and mathematically invalid.

The sentence 'Existing hyperbolic space methods often manipulate hierarchical embeddings or impose constraints to improve modality alignment [incorrect ref].' contains a literal unresolved placeholder citation marker '[incorrect ref]', indicating a fabricated or missing reference that was never properly filled in.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2, Efficient Adjustment for Hyperbolic Radius (block-diagonal matrix definition)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text defines W_s^{B-D} = diag(R_1,...,R_r) with R_i ∈ R^{(n/r)×(n/r)}, then states 'Here, r is the block size.' But by the given formula, r is the number of blocks while n/r is the actual block dimension (block size), which is consistent with Table 3's column header 'n/r' being used to denote the varying block size (values 2, 4, 8). This is an internal definitional inconsistency.

LLaVA-Next is cited as [32] in the Introduction ('LLaVA-Next [32]') but in Section 5.2 it is written as 'LLaVA-Next [39]', reusing the citation number assigned to LLaVA-1.5 ([39] = Liu et al., Improved Baselines with Visual Instruction Tuning), which is a different paper from LLaVA-NeXT [32].

The text claims 'baseline MemVP generally outperforms HyperET-enhanced LaVIN... HyperET's benefits may be dataset- and architecture-specific rather than broadly generalizable,' but Table 1 shows HyperET consistently improves every paired baseline it is applied to (LaVIN+Ours > LaVIN, MemVP+Ours > MemVP, in both 7B and 13B settings), contradicting this negative framing which compares unrelated method pairs (LaVIN+Ours vs. MemVP) rather than matched baselines.

The text states 'HyperET is trained with an extended schedule and augmented compute budget not matched in the baseline settings. Such discrepancies may contribute significantly to improved results, complicating direct attribution to HyperET alone,' which directly undermines the paper's central efficiency claim (abstract: 'roughly 1% additional parameters') and indicates an unfair, confounded comparison protocol.

The text claims 'Results were largely similar regardless of the multiplication operation used. This suggests Möbius multiplication may have limited practical impact on performance.' However, Table 3 shows +W_s^D (no ⊗_c) achieves 93.91 while +W_s^D (with ⊗_c) achieves 94.72, a 0.81-point difference, and Table 5 shows a similar gap (81.1 vs 82.3 for -⊗_c vs +W_s), contradicting the claim of similarity.

The text states 'training in Euclidean space instead of hyperbolic space leads to significantly lower performance... The observed improvement over the baseline is primarily attributable to the increased number of parameters rather than the alignment of granularity levels.' This is self-contradictory: if the Euclidean variant (which has the same added parameter count) performs significantly worse than the hyperbolic variant, the improvement cannot be attributed primarily to parameter count.
The text claims 'a 2.1% gain on TextVQA [53]', but Table 5 reports baseline TVQA = 61.3 and +W_s TVQA = 63.9, an actual gain of 2.6 points, not 2.1.

The caption states 'Top-1 accuracy is reported' for all 12 benchmarks, but the ME (MME) column reports raw scores such as 1510.7 and 1536.2, which are not percentage/Top-1 accuracy values, making the blanket caption claim inconsistent with the reported MME numbers.

The Introduction states 'HyperET introduces less than 1% of the total trainable parameters,' but Table 1 shows for LLaMA-7B configurations the added parameters are 0.05M out of 3.8M (LaVIN) and 3.9M (MemVP) baseline trainable parameters, i.e., ~1.3%, which exceeds 1% and contradicts the 'less than 1%' claim.

The statement 'Our method builds on these by preserving global hierarchy and applying hyperbolic radius adjustment, although the distinction from existing approaches remains subtle' undermines the paper's claimed novel contribution and is inconsistent with the strong efficacy claims made throughout the rest of the paper.
